newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Christopher strides past APEC dinner receiving line.
newsitem.headline: Christopher strides past APEC dinner receiving line.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher strode unsmiling past the foreign and trade ministers of the Philippines forming the receiving line at an APEC dinner on Friday night.

Other guests -- foreign and trade ministers, delegates and their wives -- attending the annual APEC meeting shook hands and chatted with their Filipino hosts, Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon and Trade Minister Cesar Bautista and their wives.
The recieving line at a ballroom of the plush Manila Hotel did not appear to notice Christopher stride past surrounded by his security men, glancing neither right nor left.
Christopher apparently did not see the receiving line.
It was a welcoming banquet for delegates at the annual meeting of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum where cooperation and goodwill has been a theme.
A top U.S. official, asked about the incident, said he was sure no insult was intended and that Christopher's party has just failed to notice the line.

The secretary of state was later seated at a round table which also included foreign ministers Qian Qichen of China, Alexander Downer of Australia, Yukihiko Ikeda of Japan and Jose Miguel Insulza of Chile.

They tucked into soup of young coconut juice and chicken stock flavoured with ginger and lemon grass, stuffed chicken with pineapple, and fresh mangoes, washed down with French Pouilly Fuisse white wine.
During the day, senior members of Christopher's official party were body-searched at the hotel and at the seafront convention centre where the APEC ministerial meeting is being held.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns, who earlier warned U.S. diplomats, journalists and others of possible attacks, described the security searches as "an unusual but rational precaution".
